column1: # The model and effort of every phase of a package, by the package's class and by the tool that
# runs it: one definition per project, read by the person in charge each time it starts a phase
# session. `ai-core phase-model` selects its execution tool, model and effort before every start
# and resume; `ai-core tool-order` persists the owner's machine-wide preference across restarts.
# Columns: tool <TAB> phase <TAB> class <TAB> model <TAB> effort
# tool    claude, codex or agy, by the name of its command on PATH. Each tool is its own ecosystem
#         with its own coordinator and models. A package stays in its coordinator's ecosystem.
#         Without a saved order a `<tool>:<model>` row routes a native-tool selection to its
#         declared destination. An explicit order governs actual execution tools. A package keeps
#         its coordinator's ecosystem and number block.
#         The issues nobody planned belong to the first tool of ECOSYSTEM_ORDER in config.env;
#         a later tool plans what the owner hands its coordinator. A tool with
# phase   coordinator (the person in charge itself), plan, re-plan (every plan session of a package
#         after its first plan: after a plan-check NO, a plan repair, an amendment, a review that
#         sends the package back to plan, but not the plan of a mechanical package sent to a
#         plan, which is its first), plan-check, build (build and test),
#         review, ui-test (the UI test and the live check), helper (a bounded task inside any phase: a pre-review of a diff, a log, a
#         screenshot, a long span; its answer is checked by the session that asked). The start
#         check is START_CHECK of config.env and has no row. The plan runs on the high-risk row
#         where an issue names a secret, a payment, a contract outward or the push gate (the
#         class line below says what outward means), else on
#         the normal-hard row, because the plan decides between those two classes. The coordinator
#         decides mechanical from the issues, before any plan: a mechanical package has no plan and
# class   mechanical (the change stays in one repository; it touches no contract between the
#         project's repositories and no contract outward; it touches no secret, no payment and not
#         the push gate; the change of all its issues together is at most 150 lines outside tests,
#         and each issue has its acceptance criteria), high-risk (security, payments,
#         contracts outward, the push gate; outward means an interface somebody outside the
#         project uses (a public API, a published package, a customer's data format), never a
#         contract between the project's own repositories), normal-hard (everything else); *
#         for every class. An issue whose plan runs on a high-risk row its tool lacks is not that
#         tool's work: it goes back to the owner.
# model   what the tool's model option takes, or `<tool>:<model>` for a phase on the named tool, using a
#         model declared by that tool in this table. agy runs at high effort, never xhigh.
#         Saving an order leaves the model rows unchanged.
# effort  what the tool takes for it (`claude --effort`, `codex -c model_reasoning_effort=`); - where
#         the model name carries it, as agy's names do.
# Every phase starts and resumes on exactly the selector's tuple. For plan-check and review,
# pass --written-by with the actual writer model; aliases and effort changes are not independence.
# A plan re-check uses plan-check and the re-plan writer; a review re-check uses review and the
# repair builder. Both keep their 100k budget and reading scope, with the selected row's effort.
# A refusal waits; there is no prose fallback to the writer. A project harness replaces the whole
# file with its own: the same name replaces.
